user.title: Sonance DSP amplifier
user.description: Enter the IP address of the amplifier. It will be identified by its serial number, so a DHCP address change will not orphan this entry.

data_description.host: The amplifier's IP address or hostname.
data_description.port: TCP control port. Leave at 52000 unless it has been changed.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the amplifier. Check the IP address and that nothing else holds a control connection — the amplifier accepts only one at a time.

abort.unique_id_mismatch: The amplifier at this address reports a different serial number than the one configured.

init.title: Sonance DSP options
init.description:
The amplifier's range is -70 to +12 dB. The maximum below is the level reached at 100% on the volume slider; the default of 0 dB leaves +12 dB of headroom deliberately out of reach. The amplifier keeps its own per-channel ceiling too, and a zone is capped by whichever is lower.

Linking a source to a media player lets a zone show what is playing on it. The amplifier only knows it is amplifying a line input; the player feeding that input is the only thing that knows the track.

data_description.input_link_1: The media player connected to input 1. Its title, artist and artwork appear on any zone playing this source.
data_description.input_link_2: The media player connected to input 2. Its title, artist and artwork appear on any zone playing this source.
data_description.input_link_3: The media player connected to input 3. Its title, artist and artwork appear on any zone playing this source.
data_description.input_link_4: The media player connected to input 4. Its title, artist and artwork appear on any zone playing this source.
data_description.max_db: Level reached at 100% on the volume slider.
data_description.scan_interval: How often to poll the amplifier.

unknown_source.message: {source} is not an input on this amplifier. Available sources: {sources}.

amp_did_not_wake.message: The amplifier did not finish waking within {seconds} seconds. Check that it is powered and that its Auto On method is Power Button.

amp_wake_recently_failed.message: The amplifier did not wake on the last attempt, so it will not be tried again for {seconds} seconds unless it is seen on first. Try again later.

amp_power_unknown.message: The amplifier did not say whether it is on or in standby, so nothing was switched. Try again.

zone_power_not_confirmed.message: Zone {zone} did not report {state} after two attempts.

mute_unknown.message: Zone {zone} did not say whether it is muted, so its volume was not changed: on this amplifier a volume change un-mutes. Try again.

transport_zone_off.message: {entity_id} is off. Playback belongs to its source, so play, pause and skip would act on every other zone playing it; switch the zone on first.

transport_unavailable.message: {entity_id} has no linked player that offers this control.

auto_on_method.title: {name}: Auto On is {method}, not Power Button
auto_on_method.description: Home Assistant controls this amplifier's power, which is only safe with its Auto On method set to **Power Button**. With {method}, the amplifier can wake zones by itself. Set it in the amplifier's web UI, under General Settings.

channel_sleep.title: {name}: sleep is on for some channels
channel_sleep.description: Sleep is on for {channels}. Home Assistant controls this amplifier's power, and sleep would switch zones off without it knowing. Set every channel's sleep to **OFF** in the amplifier's web UI, under General Settings.

turn_on_volume.title: {name}: turn-on volume is not {silent} dB
turn_on_volume.description: For about a second after a zone is switched on, the amplifier plays it **unmuted at its turn-on volume**, whatever its mute. Set the turn-on volume to {silent} dB so that second is silent; Home Assistant then restores the zone's own level. Not yet at {silent} dB: {zones}. Set it in the amplifier's web UI, under In/Out Settings.
